I have had some thoughts recently about XT and I propose a deal. I think there is a very rational option in which every party will be better off.

Let's say XT get's a majority. It doesn't even have to have the 750/1000 blocks yet, just a majority. The sensible thing for Bitcoin Core is to implement BIP 101 as well. What else can they do? The miners have spoken and they want to swich. The only chance the Bitcoin Core developers have to stay relevant is to adopt the change too. The XT developers want BIP 101, but they don't want a fork if they can prevent it. So the logical conclusion? Merge XT and it's improvements into Core, make the XT developers also developers of Core and encourage miners to swich back to Core. This way a fork can be prevented but a decision has still been made democratically. Also, there would be no confusion about altcoins or which is the 'real' Bitcoin. Furthermore, the fact that a forked would've occured shows that the miners can decide what happens, which will make sure that the developers will act in their favour.

If the developers can set aside their grudges, this might be in everyone's own interest. It would be a democratic victory, as well as a diplomatic one. What do you think?

The creators of XT are Core developers with commit access. The reason why BIP 101 is not merged in Core is because the majority of Core developers is against the merge.

The Core developers have been thinking about the blocksize issue way longer that the recent revolts. All of them (IIRC) are in favor of bigger blocks, but think 8MB blocks now and 8GB blocks by 2036 is too high. Especially that last one. BIP 101 defines a growth curve that is very steep. 2036 is a long time from now, but 8GB blocks surely look scary.

There are other proposals that describe a more dynamic blocksize increase, depending on the latest blocks or on mining consensus.
